title: Doro Wat
subtitle: Ethiopian slow-cooked chicken stew with berbere spices
excerpt: A deeply spiced Ethiopian chicken stew made with slowly caramelised onions, berbere-inspired spices, and ghee, finished with hard-boiled eggs simmered in the sauce. This is one of the great dishes of East African cooking.
sourceNotes: Doro wat is the national dish of Ethiopia and one of the most important dishes in Ethiopian cuisine. It is traditionally prepared for celebrations and religious holidays, cooked slowly over low heat for several hours. The berbere spice blend that gives the dish its heat and complexity is a central element of both Ethiopian and Eritrean cooking.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Doro wat tastes better the next day once the spices have had time to develop.

content.text: This recipe uses sweet paprika, smoked paprika, chilli flakes, and warming spices as a base for the berbere blend, since a pre-made berbere spice mix is not in the pantry list. The combination gives a close result. The key to doro wat is patience with the onions: they need a full 30 to 40 minutes to cook down into a thick, almost jam-like base before anything else is added.

items.prepNote: hard-boiled, peeled, and pierced all over with a fork

content.text: Cook the onions in a dry stockpot over medium-low heat for 10 minutes, stirring often. Add the ghee and continue cooking for a further 25 to 30 minutes, stirring regularly, until very soft, deeply golden, and reduced to about a third of the original volume.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 3 minutes. Add all the spices and the tomato puree. Stir well and cook for 2 more minutes.

Add the scored chicken legs and 250 ml of water. Stir to coat the chicken in the spiced onion base. Bring to a simmer, cover, and cook on low heat for 35 to 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the lid and add the hard-boiled eggs. Simmer uncovered for 10 minutes until the sauce thickens and the eggs take on colour from the sauce. Season with salt.
Serve with injera if available, or with rice.

items.symptom: Onion base is catching and burning
items.cause: Heat too high during the long cook
items.fix: Keep heat on low and add a splash of water if it sticks.

items.cause: Cooked with the lid on the whole time
items.fix: Remove the lid for the last 10 to 15 minutes to let it firm up.

items.cause: Spices not cooked long enough in the fat
items.fix: Cook the spice paste for a full 2 minutes before adding the chicken.
